hints: Keep both nucleon number and charge balanced on the two sides of the nuclear equation.
In β+ decay, the proton number falls by one and the emitted particles include a positron and an electron neutrino.
walkthrough: The nucleon number remains 18, while the proton number must decrease from 9 to 8, giving oxygen-18 as the daughter nucleus.
A β+ particle has nucleon number 0 and charge +1, so it accounts for the charge change.
An electron neutrino is emitted in β+ decay to conserve lepton number.
The completed equation is ¹⁸₉F → ¹⁸₈O + ⁰₊₁β + ⁰₀νₑ.

ai_rubric.observable: Includes an electron neutrino with the β+ decay.
Includes a positron, ⁰₊₁β or equivalent.
Gives oxygen-18, ¹⁸₈O, as the daughter nucleus.

hints: A β+ decay turns a proton into a neutron, so compare their up- and down-quark compositions.
A proton has uud and a neutron has udd, so identify the single quark flavour change.
walkthrough: A proton has quark composition uud, while a neutron has udd.
In β+ decay, one up quark changes into a down quark.
The required flavour change is up quark to down quark.

ai_rubric.observable: States that an up quark changes to a down quark.

hints: Compare the largest possible charge from a quark–antiquark pair with the stated −2e charge.
A meson contains one quark and one antiquark, while a baryon contains three (anti)quarks.
walkthrough: A meson has one quark and one antiquark, so its possible net charge is 0 or ±e; it cannot have charge −2e.
A charge of −2e requires three antiquarks, each of charge −2e/3.
The hadron is therefore a baryon, specifically an antibaryon under the broad three-(anti)quark classification.

ai_rubric.observable: Explains that a −2e hadron must contain three antiquarks because a meson can have only 0 or ±e, or gives the equivalent quark-charge argument.
Identifies the hadron as a baryon.

hints: A total charge of −2e from three constituents requires each constituent to have charge −2e/3.
Use the antiquarks of the +2e/3 quark flavours.
walkthrough: An antiup, anticharm or antitop quark each has charge −2e/3.
Any three of these antiquarks have total charge 3(−2e/3) = −2e.
One valid composition is antiup–antiup–antiup (ūūū); mixtures of antiup, anticharm and antitop are also valid.

ai_rubric.observable: Gives any three-quark composition chosen from antiup, anticharm and antitop quarks.
